name: Storm's Stork
rangeDescription: Lowlands of borneo, eastern sumatra, and malay peninsula
description: Small dark stork with a white neck patch and a bright red bill. Also note bright yellow skin around the eyes.

name: Hawaiian Duck
rangeDescription: Hawaiian islands (kauai and oahu)
description: A medium-sized duck, similar to female Mallard in appearance, but smaller and darker. Males lack the green head and curled black tail feathers of male Mallards.

name: Fire-fronted Serin
rangeDescription: Mountains of türkiye to western china; winters to israel
description: Sprightly and vividly-colored little finch with a black head and a fiery orange patch on the forehead. Sexes are similar, though female tends to have a smaller forehead patch than the male.

name: Letter-winged Kite
rangeDescription: Interior of australia; disperses irregularly to coasts
description: Small, striking gray and white raptor with black shoulder patches. Underparts white with two black patches on underwing extending from

name: Albertine Boubou
rangeDescription: Eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, rwanda, and burundi
description: Mid-sized bushshrike that is completely black. Found in the undergrowth of humid forest at higher elevations.

name: Solomons White-eye
rangeDescription: Solomon islands (kolombangara, vonavona, kohinggo, new georgia, vangunu, and nggatokae)
description: Small olive-yellow warbler-like bird, restricted to a handful of islands in the New Georgia Group, in the west-central Solomon Islands. Formerly lumped with Dark-eyed White-eye; note present species’ bright white eye-ring and yellow belly.

name: Western Bristlebird
rangeDescription: Coastal heaths of southwestern western australia (east of albany)
description: Small, long-tailed terrestrial bird of dense coastal heath in a very restricted portion of southwestern Western Australia. Grayish brown with pale streaking above, similar but lighter pattern below, with dark red eye, reddish wing, pale moustachial marks, and long, graduated rusty tail.

name: Brown Firefinch
rangeDescription: Angola to democratic republic of the congo, zambia, southern tanzania, northern namibia, and northern zimbabwe
description: This is the darkest and dullest firefinch, the only species without a red or pink rump. Both sexes have red in the bill.

name: Long-billed Crow
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (morotai, halmahera, kayoa, bacan, obi, and kasiruta)
description: A distinctive crow with a strikingly long bill, noticeable even in flight. Adults have purple-glossed blackish plumage and a prominent pale eye.

name: Crested Hornero
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: A mostly terrestrial and chunky light brown bird of the north and central Chaco, from central Argentina to Western Paraguay and extreme SE Bolivia. Distinguished from Rufous Hornero by crest, from Lark-like Brushrunner by plain plumage, and from Cachalotes by dull plumage, smaller bill and size, and dark iris.

name: Chilean Pigeon
rangeDescription: Araucaria and nothofagus forest and adjacent fields of central and southern chile and adjacent argentina
description: Only large native pigeon in its range. Locally fairly common in temperate rainforest, farmland with wooded patches, and matorral with taller trees.

name: Rusty-flanked Crake
rangeDescription: Locally in wetlands of northern venezuela north of the río orinoco
description: Small unbarred rufous crake with greenish bill and white central underparts. Sexes similar.

name: Collared Crow
rangeDescription: Central and eastern china to northern vietnam; hainan and taiwan
description: By far the most distinctive crow of farmland, fields, and other open spaces: adults black with white hindneck connecting to white breast band. Superficially similar to adult Daurian Jackdaw, but the latter is more compact and smaller, with pale plumage extending through the belly.

name: Moheli Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Mohéli (comoros)
description: Small, compact dark owl with small ear tufts. The overall coloration is variable, and can be rufous or dark brown.

name: White-lined Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (sandstones of western arnhem land, northern territory)
description: Rather plain medium-sized honeyeater found in sandstone escarpment and gorge country of western Arnhem Land, including the sandstone areas of Kakadu National Park and Katherine Gorge. Upperparts uniformly gray-green, underparts pale with diffuse gray streaks on chest.

name: Roberts's Warbler
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern zimbabwe and adjacent southwestern mozambique
description: A dull gray-brown prinia-like warbler with a long and graduated tail, pale gray throat, ochre eyes, and pinkish legs. Pairs and family groups may join mixed-species flocks, foraging studiously through the lower branches of forest, undergrowth and bracken, forest edge, and occasionally pausing to chatter in unison.

name: Red-breasted Meadowlark
rangeDescription: Southwestern costa rica to trinidad and the guianas, amazonian brazil, and northwestern bolivia
description: This attractive meadowlark is found in open fields. It often perches conspicuously atop grasses or small bushes.

name: Fernwren
rangeDescription: Montane wet tropical zone of northeastern queensland
description: Small scrubwren-like bird found in wet rainforests at higher elevations in the Atherton Tablelands of far northern Queensland. Adult entirely brown except for white throat, black bib, and faint pale supercilium.

name: Reischek's Parakeet
rangeDescription: Antipodes islands
description: A medium-sized, emerald-green parakeet endemic to the Antipodes Islands, including smaller outer islands. Recognized by its distinctive bright red crown and small red patches behind the eyes.

name: Lord Howe Rail
rangeDescription: Highlands of lord howe island (endangered)
description: A long-necked and short-tailed rail with a long decurved bill. Uniformly brownish red, sometimes with variable barring on underside and flanks.
